newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rise in U.S. rates to benefit Hong Kong -- Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Rise in U.S. rates to benefit Hong Kong -- Salomon.

text.p: Rising inflation will cause real interest rates in Hong Kong to fall this year despite an expected increase of up to 50 basis points in U.S. rates, Salomon Brothers says.
"The modest decline in real rates is likely to give further momentum to Hong Kong's cyclical recovery," Salomon said in a research report dated January 27.
But Salomon is holding its gross domestic product forecast for the territory steady at 5.5 percent following its five percent forecast for 1996.
Low inventories and robust economic growth suggest the U.S. economy will continue to expand into the first quarter of this year, it said.
While the strength is unlikely to last into the second half, accumulated wage pressure will probably prompt a moderately tighter monetary policy during the year, Salomon said.
A rise of 25 to 50 basis points will cause a similar rise in Hong Kong's nominal interest rates.

"The prospect of rising nominal interest rates appears to be a major concern to investors as they fear that expected monetary tightening may slow the pace of Hong Kong's economic recovery," Salomon wrote.
"However, we believe this expected rate increase is unlikely to be a key concern, as Hong Kong's real interest rates are still likely to fall in 1997."
Salomon defines real interest rates as nominal interest rates minus the consumer price index (A), Hong Kong's broadest measure of inflation.
Hong Kong's inflation started to trend upward in the third quarter of 1996, with the growth of CPI (A) rising for five consecutive months to 6.7 percent in December 1996 from five percent in August.
For full-year 1996, inflation stood at six percent and Salomon expects it to rise to seven percent in 1997. As a result, the prime rate is likely to fall by 75 basis points to 1.75 percent this year.
"Even assuming an aggressive 50-basis point increase in the nominal prime rate to nine percent, the real prime rate is still likely to fall by 50 basis points to two percent in 1997," Salomon said.

Pressuring inflation forecasts are an expected rise in rent prices following last year's 30-percent gain in property prices, higher inflation in food prices and general price increases as consumption growth improves, Salomom said.

"In addition to improving the labour market, increasing consumer confidence and the positive wealth effect stemming from the rally of local stock and property markets, the expectation of a moderately falling real interest rate is likely to help sustain the cyclical recovery in consumption in 1997," it said.
